pages.name: Weldroot
pages.description:
Trace paths through the root system of alloy trees.

ℹ️​NOTE: not all connections are guaranteed in the same cycle​, but there are always some. Finish the cycle when you can’t find more connections.​

The game continues until you run out of cycles. Try to get as high a score as possible before that happens.

Controls

Left- or right-click to rotate roots.

Credits & Attribution

See the game's Credits panel.
pages.short: Trace paths through the root system of alloy trees
pages.themeJustification: Those are some weird trees, but they're still trees

users.name: Cosmo
users.bio:
Hiya, I'm Cosmo!

I'm a 19 year old nerdy trans girl game dev who does an unhealthy amount of game jams, and makes an endless stream of cool vaguely finished projects.

I primarily stick with Unity for my engine of choice. I only have a couple years of experience under my belt, but I've been making games in some form or another since I was just a kid.

Happy to answer any questions or chat about technical nerdy stuff, and I'm trying to make most of my source code public on my newer games, if you'd like to poke around at my projects.

Dreaming to make it as a real indie game developer someday, but I'll stick to my random silly projects for now.

Hope you enjoy my shenanigans! <3

author.name: JcupDev
author.bio: Tworkin on Fabled Footy and jamming

comments.content:
Fun pipe connection puzzles! It was a cool challenge trying to find the optimal paths to minimize the amount of cycles. Once you get to the part with 5 blue connections though, that challenge sort of disappears since most of the difficulty comes from having multiple colors to funnel.\
\
The sfx for snapping the roots together is satisfying. The music is calm which fits the mood nicely but the sine wave bassline sounds a bit de-tuned and stiff. I’d suggest having the bassline’s notes breathe in and out (volume automation and reverb).\
\
Overall, awesome experience guys! I enjoyed this one :)

author.name: nojoule
author.bio:
Programmer, GameDev & Artist. Creating Game Assets for Godot.\
\
Check out my website: [nojoule.com](http://nojoule.com)\
My game assets: [nojoule.itch.io](http://nojoule.itch.io)\
I also make some YouTube videos: [www.youtube.com/@nojoule](https://www.youtube.com/@nojoule)

comments.content:
I think you mentioned in the server it’s your first Godot game, congratulations :) 

I really like how the main mechanic is made. It’s smooth and has a nice interactive “yummy’ factor to it.

```
No goblins and no godly widget. Literally unplayable.
```

author.name: XpMonster
author.bio:
Making games and publishing under Empyreans :)
https://www.twitch.tv/xpmonsterx

comments.content:
It was a great little puzzle game. unfortunately as you noted, it’s not always possible to get all connections in one cycle, therefore getting the highest score is up to chance.\
Very clean design and I love the small details with the connections wiggling a little bit when they connect.\
The music is nice and relaxing and the soundscape is great.

What a delightful game! I racked my brain trying to get all the paths in a single move. I haven't managed them all yet, but I saved the game here so I can crush your challenge, :D

Congratulations to the team!

author.name: EulerMoises
author.bio:
A musician passionate about video games since 1986, learning to compose soundtracks and produce sound effects. I love pixel art and whenever I can, I create the art for my game jams. My current prank is learning to program to create my own little games for gamejams, and I must confess that it's quite difficult to gain XP in this side quest...

author.bio: I’m Steve of Steves Games and I love making stuff.

comments.content: Very clever puzzle. Enjoyed the satisfying chaining of bubbles when the route was completed. I think the clever part here is making sure that all the routes were filled so no cycle was wasted. I liked it
Very statisfying game to play! I love the connecting part especially!

users.name: Cosmo
users.bio:
Hiya, I'm Cosmo!

I'm a 19 year old nerdy trans girl game dev who does an unhealthy amount of game jams, and makes an endless stream of cool vaguely finished projects.

I primarily stick with Unity for my engine of choice. I only have a couple years of experience under my belt, but I've been making games in some form or another since I was just a kid.

Happy to answer any questions or chat about technical nerdy stuff, and I'm trying to make most of my source code public on my newer games, if you'd like to poke around at my projects.

Dreaming to make it as a real indie game developer someday, but I'll stick to my random silly projects for now.

Hope you enjoy my shenanigans! <3

author.name: JcupDev
author.bio: Tworkin on Fabled Footy and jamming

comments.content:
Fun pipe connection puzzles! It was a cool challenge trying to find the optimal paths to minimize the amount of cycles. Once you get to the part with 5 blue connections though, that challenge sort of disappears since most of the difficulty comes from having multiple colors to funnel.\
\
The sfx for snapping the roots together is satisfying. The music is calm which fits the mood nicely but the sine wave bassline sounds a bit de-tuned and stiff. I’d suggest having the bassline’s notes breathe in and out (volume automation and reverb).\
\
Overall, awesome experience guys! I enjoyed this one :)

comments.content:
It was a great little puzzle game. unfortunately as you noted, it’s not always possible to get all connections in one cycle, therefore getting the highest score is up to chance.\
Very clean design and I love the small details with the connections wiggling a little bit when they connect.\
The music is nice and relaxing and the soundscape is great.

What a delightful game! I racked my brain trying to get all the paths in a single move. I haven't managed them all yet, but I saved the game here so I can crush your challenge, :D

Congratulations to the team!
